decision: For WF-047, mirror room documents into CRM files, which shape should the build take: a new backend/dsr/crm_file_sync domain package plus the plugin on /api/wf-047, and which of the six open decisions the research left unresolved should be resolved how?

state.name: Mirror room documents into CRM files
state.criticality: supplementary. Why: 'Document mirroring into CRM files; duplicative by design.'

sourced_half_of_the_workflow.upload: HubSpot: 'Files can be uploaded using a multipart/form-data POST request to files/2026-09/files with the following fields' including field 'file'. 'While a specific folder ID is not required at upload, it's recommended to upload files into a folder and not the root directory.' 'Uploaded files are subject to the limits and supported formats'. 'Folder requirements at upload are subject to change.'
sourced_half_of_the_workflow.file_property: HubSpot property types: 'file | Allows for a file to be uploaded on a record or via a form. Stores a file ID.'
sourced_half_of_the_workflow.attach: HubSpot files guide: 'Attach files to records using the notes APIs.'
sourced_half_of_the_workflow.salesforce: Binary content can be submitted base64-encoded in an sObject body. The blob page was readable only as a link index and no payload example is quoted.
sourced_half_of_the_workflow.gaps: Salesforce Files (ContentVersion/ContentDocument/ContentDocumentLink) could not be sourced: every candidate resources-content* URL returned 404. Microsoft Dataverse file/image columns and annotation/attachment tables could not be sourced: the doc pages returned 404. Only HubSpot's Files API is fully documented for this workflow.
sourced_half_of_the_workflow.idempotency: User-flow step 4: 'The room stores crm_file_id on the asset row, so re-uploads are skipped and revisions create a new file.'
sourced_half_of_the_workflow.extensibility: A third-party connector supports any file-capable CRM by implementing two methods: upload(bytes) -> fileId and attach(fileId, recordId). The room's asset table holds the vendor-agnostic crm_file_id slot, so file sync state survives connector swaps.

unsourced_and_therefore_chosen_not_inven: A Salesforce file payload. The spec forbids inventing one, so Salesforce is implemented as a base64 sObject body only if a payload can be derived; otherwise the connector refuses with a named gap.
A Dataverse file column. Unsourced. The connector refuses with a named gap.
A schedule for the reconciliation pass. The spec gives the rule ('find room assets with no crm_file_id and push them') and no cadence.

existing_crm_packages_on_main_and_why_no.crm_upsert: Batch-upsert of engagement rows keyed on external id. Has a Transport seam, capabilities, payloads, runs. Sends JSON bodies to record endpoints. No binary body, no folder, no file id.
existing_crm_packages_on_main_and_why_no.crm_provisioning: Creates CRM objects, properties and alternate keys. Has a gateway simulated in the audited store. Owns crm_remote_object, crm_remote_property, crm_remote_key. No file.
existing_crm_packages_on_main_and_why_no.crm_integration: Read-only field-scoped paged read of deal, account and contact. WF-042, the dependency. No write of any kind, no file.
existing_crm_packages_on_main_and_why_no.fieldmap: Field mapping between room and CRM columns. No file.
existing_crm_packages_on_main_and_why_no.library: WF-007 content library with a multipart ingest of bytes plus a metadata JSON part. That is an inbound ingest into the room, not an outbound push into a CRM, and it holds no CRM record or file id.
existing_crm_packages_on_main_and_why_no.grep_result: grep for crm_file_id, files/2026, multipart, upload(bytes), attach(file_id, recordId) across backend/dsr returned no CRM file-upload path. The only multipart callers are the inbound library ingest, the WF-039 Dataverse changeset writer and the WF-082 signed webhook verifier.
existing_crm_packages_on_main_and_why_no.conclusion: Nothing on main covers outbound file upload plus attach. The issue's own rule allows a new package only in this case, and this is that case.

state.constraint_from_the_brief: Prefer extending an existing CRM package over a new one if the subject matches; create crm_file_sync/ only if nothing covers file upload/attach. The grep above is the evidence that nothing does.

the_six_open_decisions_this_gate_must_se.one_package_or_two: New crm_file_sync package versus extending crm_upsert. crm_upsert's transport is built for JSON record bodies with no file concept and its batch semantics are about upsert rows, not uploads.
the_six_open_decisions_this_gate_must_se.revision_detection: The spec says 're-uploads are skipped and revisions create a new file' and does not say how a revision is detected. Candidates: (a) the store's envelope revision counter, which changes on every update including a metadata edit that does not change bytes; (b) a content digest of the asset bytes plus the filename, stored next to crm_file_id, so only a byte-level change creates a new file.
the_six_open_decisions_this_gate_must_se.reconcile_schedule: The spec gives the rule and no cadence. Candidates: (a) a poll route a scheduler calls, never a thread, matching how crm_backfill already derives its floor; (b) an interval timer inside the package.
the_six_open_decisions_this_gate_must_se.folder_id_configuration: HubSpot recommends a folder, warns 'Folder requirements at upload are subject to change', and says a folder id is not required. Candidates: (a) folder id is optional per connection, resolved at upload time, and a connection with none is valid and documented as uploading to the root; (b) a folder id is mandatory and a connection without one is refused.
the_six_open_decisions_this_gate_must_se.attach_mode: The spec allows 'a file-type property value, or into a note attached to the record'. HubSpot's own words are 'Attach files to records using the notes APIs' and file properties 'store a file ID'. Candidates: (a) both modes, notes the default; (b) file property only; (c) note only.
the_six_open_decisions_this_gate_must_se.default_automation: The spec offers event-driven and a scheduled pass. Candidates: (a) event-driven by default with the reconciliation pass available and optional; (b) scheduled by default; (c) both always on.

state.network_posture: No module in this feature opens a socket by default. The connector is a Protocol with two methods, the default implementation is a local simulation that holds vendor file state in the audited store, and a deployment can substitute its own connector. This matches crm_provisioning's gateway and crm_upsert's SimulatedTransport.
state.schema_posture: Ordinary JSON in records.data. Collections planned: crm_file_connection, crm_file_asset, crm_file_mirror. The asset row holds the vendor-agnostic crm_file_id slot, so sync state survives a connector swap. No migration and no typed column.
state.audit_posture: Every write goes through AuditedDatabase with a source string naming a route the plugin actually serves, in the form 'POST /api/wf-047/...' derived from router.prefix.
acceptance_criteria_from_the_issue: FEATURE exports id, name and a ticket-derived prefix /api/wf-047
mounted by discovery alone, api.py not edited
domain module imports nothing but the store; no dsr.api and no bare sqlite3
records are ordinary JSON in records.data, no migration, no typed column
every write goes through AuditedDatabase and its audit row names a served route
seed(db, context) returns a cp1252-encodable string naming the states it created
the frontend page uses shared components and no emoji as an icon
tests pass alone and under pytest-xdist with no order dependence
ruff check and ruff format --check pass from the repository root
state.hard_constraint_from_the_issue: The spec's Why field says this workflow is duplicative by design, so an existing file-mirroring path must be checked before a second one is added. The grep above is that check and it came back empty.

reason: chose 'build_this_shape' but confidence 0.55 < 0.75; insufficient evidence to gate on

package_shape.instructions: Should WF-047 live in a new backend/dsr/crm_file_sync package or extend an existing CRM package such as crm_upsert? Weigh the brief's prefer-extend rule against the grep showing that no existing CRM package covers outbound binary file upload plus attach.

criteria.new_crm_file_sync_package: Create backend/dsr/crm_file_sync/ with vocabulary, errors, connectors, assets, engine and inferences. Justified because crm_upsert's transport carries JSON record bodies with no binary body, no folder and no file id, and because the spec's own extensibility clause asks for a two-method connector interface that no existing package models. Cost: one more top-level package.
criteria.extend_crm_upsert: Add file upload and attach to crm_upsert. Cost: that package's transport, capability and batch model is about upsert rows keyed on external ids. A file upload is a different request shape with a different idempotency key and a folder concept, so the addition would either bend that model or sit beside it inside one package, which is the second CRM package the issue warns against.
criteria.extend_ds_r_crm: Add file support to dsr/crm, which currently pushes room events out over webhooks and automations. Cost: that package sends signed JSON envelopes to subscriber URLs. A multipart file upload is not an event delivery, and its channel carries no secrets this feature needs to touch.

revision_detection.instructions: How should this workflow detect that a room asset is a new revision that must produce a new CRM file? The spec says re-uploads are skipped and revisions create a new file but does not say how a revision is detected.

criteria.content_digest: Store a digest of the asset bytes plus the filename next to crm_file_id on the asset row. Skip when the digest is unchanged. A byte-level change produces a new file id; a metadata edit that does not change the bytes does not. Cost: the digest must be computed and stored, and a room that rewrites identical bytes re-uploads only if the digest algorithm changes.
criteria.envelope_revision_counter: Use the record envelope's revision counter, which the store increments on every update. Cost: any metadata edit bumps it, so renaming a document or changing its folder uploads a new CRM file the buyer never asked for. The counter measures writes, not content.
criteria.explicit_revision_flag: The room sets a revision marker on the asset whenever it intends a new file. Cost: the caller has to remember, and a generated asset that forgets to set it is never pushed again, which is a silent failure the reconciliation pass would then push anyway.

reconcile_schedule.instructions: How should the reconciliation pass that finds room assets with no crm_file_id be driven? The spec gives the rule and no cadence.

criteria.poll_route_no_thread: Expose the pass as a route an external scheduler calls, and derive the recommended cadence from the vendor's own limits rather than installing a timer. Nothing in the package starts a thread. Cost: a deployment must schedule it.
criteria.interval_timer_in_package: The package starts a background timer. Cost: a thread inside a request-serving process is order-dependent in tests, runs in every worker under a multi-process deployment, and cannot be paused.
criteria.on_read_reconciliation: Run the pass whenever the documents page is read. Cost: a read that writes is a surprising side effect, and a page refresh becomes an unbounded upload burst.

folder_id_configuration.instructions: How should the optional CRM folder id be configured, given HubSpot recommends a folder, warns 'Folder requirements at upload are subject to change', and says a folder id is not required at upload?

criteria.optional_per_connection: Folder id is optional on a connection, resolved at upload time. A connection with none uploads to the root and the mirror row records that the recommendation was not followed. A folder id that the vendor later rejects produces a named failure on the mirror row rather than a silent fall back to root.
criteria.mandatory_folder_id: Refuse a connection with no folder id. Cost: the vendor does not require one and says so, so this refuses a configuration the vendor accepts, and the warning about changing folder requirements would then break every upload when a folder is retired.
criteria.hardcode_one_folder: Ship one folder id in the build. Cost: it is a tenant-specific value with no source, and it would be wrong for every other tenant.

attach_mode.instructions: How should a returned file id be written back to the CRM record? The spec allows 'a file-type property value, or into a note attached to the record'.

criteria.both_modes_note_default: Support both, with the note the default because the vendor's own words are 'Attach files to records using the notes APIs'. A connection may choose the file-type property, whose documented behaviour is 'Stores a file ID'. Cost: two code paths and two shapes on the mirror row.
criteria.file_property_only: Write only a file-type property. Cost: the vendor documents that an attachment to a record is done through the notes APIs, so this relies on a property the tenant may not have created and does not create a timeline entry.
criteria.note_only: Write only a note. Cost: the spec names both and a tenant that configured a file-type property gets no use from it.

default_automation.instructions: Which of the spec's two automation modes should be the default: event-driven mirroring on asset change, or the scheduled reconciliation pass?

criteria.event_driven_reconcile_optional: Mirror on asset create and update by default, and leave the reconciliation pass as an available route a scheduler may call. Cost: an asset that missed its event is not pushed until someone schedules the pass.
criteria.scheduled_by_default: The reconciliation pass runs on a schedule by default. Cost: the spec calls the pass a reconciliation, and a workflow that uploads every unmirrored asset on a timer surprises a tenant whose room holds assets the rep never meant to publish.
criteria.both_always_on: Both run at once. Cost: the same asset can be pushed twice in the window where an event and a pass overlap, and the idempotency guarantee then becomes the only thing standing between a tenant and duplicate files.

verdict.instructions: Is this shape the right one to build for WF-047: a new crm_file_sync domain package, a plugin on /api/wf-047 with a two-method connector interface and a local simulated connector, content-digest revision detection, a poll route for reconciliation with no thread, an optional per-connection folder id, both attach modes with the note as default, and event-driven mirroring as the default automation?

criteria.build_this_shape: Yes. Every sourced rule in the spec is implemented, every unsourced area is refused by name rather than invented, the package choice is supported by the duplication grep, and the default choices are the ones the vendor's own documentation supports.
criteria.needs_revision: No. One of the six decisions is wrong and must be changed before the build starts. Name which one and what it should be instead.
criteria.unusable: The shape cannot serve this workflow and needs a different foundation.

decision: Re-gate for WF-047 after the first gate returned uncertain. The six component decisions were settled with high confidence, but the composite verdict was split 0.70 build versus 0.30 needs_revision. This gate supplies the evidence the first one lacked: the vendor-coverage decision that was never put to a gate, and the three specific weaknesses a reviewer could name against this shape.

prior_gate.how_to_read_this: Jev did not dissent from any single component. It would not certify the bundle. The disagreement is therefore with the bundle as a whole, so this gate tests the bundle against its three named weaknesses rather than asking the six questions again.

weakness_one_vendor_coverage.the_fact: The spec's gaps block say: 'Salesforce Files (ContentVersion / ContentDocument / ContentDocumentLink) could not be sourced - every candidate resources-content* URL returned 404. Microsoft Dataverse file/image columns and annotation/attachment tables could not be sourced - the corresponding doc pages returned 404. Only HubSpot's Files API is fully documented for this workflow.'
weakness_one_vendor_coverage.what_salesforce_does_say: The spec's apis_hit list carries one Salesforce line: 'binary content can be submitted base64-encoded in an sObject body (Binary Data / blob page was reachable) - used for small generated assets.' The evidence block adds: 'Using sObject Collections to Insert a Collection of Blob Records' and 'Using sObject Collections to insert blob data requires more values in the attributes map', and then says '(The blob page was readable only as a link index; no payload example is quoted here.)'
weakness_one_vendor_coverage.the_tension: Shipping a Salesforce blob payload means writing a body the research explicitly did not quote, and the issue's own instruction is 'Do not invent a payload.' Not shipping it means a tenant on Salesforce gets nothing from this workflow even though the spec names Salesforce as one of the three systems.

the_three_ways_out.hubspot_only_named_refusal: Implement the connector interface and the HubSpot connector. Salesforce and Dataverse are registered as known systems whose file support is refused by name, carrying the spec's own gap text, so a tenant on either sees why rather than a silent absence.
the_three_ways_out.salesforce_base64_from_the_quoted_lines: Implement a Salesforce connector that base64-encodes the bytes into an sObject body using the two sentences the research does quote, and records the whole request as an inference. Cost: the quoted lines name the collection operation and say a blob insert 'requires more values in the attributes map' without saying which, so the body would be partly invented.
the_three_ways_out.ship_a_transport_seam_only: Model upload and attach as the two-method interface with no vendor implementation at all, and let a deployment supply its own. Cost: the feature has nothing to demonstrate, and a seeded demo nobody can review is what FEATURE-CONTRACT.md calls a feature nobody can review.

weakness_two_the_simulated_connector.the_fact: This product holds no CRM credentials, so the connector cannot call a vendor. The default connector must be local.
weakness_two_the_simulated_connector.what_the_precedent_does: crm_provisioning simulates the vendor inside the audited store in three collections and documents that the simulation exists so idempotency is testable rather than assertable. crm_upsert ships ScriptedTransport and SimulatedTransport and records that a simulated confirmation is never readable as a real one.
weakness_two_the_simulated_connector.what_would_make_this_weak: A simulation that invents a vendor response shape the research did not quote. The mitigation already in the plan is that every simulated row records 'simulated' on it, the mirror row names the connector that served it, and the vocabulary route publishes which vendors are simulated and which are refused.
weakness_two_the_simulated_connector.the_sourced_shape_available: HubSpot's upload response is not quoted in the spec beyond 'the returned file id'. So the simulation returns a file id and records the folder it was given, and no other vendor field is invented.

weakness_three_what_crm_file_id_is_worth.the_fact: The spec's job for this workflow is narrow: store a file, get an id, put the id in a property. Its own Extensibility field says a third-party connector supports any file-capable CRM through two methods.
weakness_three_what_crm_file_id_is_worth.the_dependency: The issue names #173 WF-042 as the dependency because it 'provisions the room's CRM deal, account and contact records. Without it, this workflow has no contact or deal record to own the attachment, so the returned file id has nowhere to be written.' WF-042 is merged on main and provisions identities holding account_id, contact_id and deal_id.
weakness_three_what_crm_file_id_is_worth.how_the_build_uses_it: A connection names which CRM object owns the attachment: deal, contact or account. The mirror reads the owning record id from the room's connection row rather than reaching into WF-042's tables, so this feature keeps working when WF-042's storage changes. That keeps the dependency directional: WF-047 reads an id, it does not require WF-042's engine.
weakness_three_what_crm_file_id_is_worth.what_would_make_this_weak: A build that imports dsr.crm_integration.engine and calls it. The brief forbids the domain module importing anything but the store, so the id is carried on this feature's own connection row and nothing else is imported.

the_shape_being_gated.package: backend/dsr/crm_file_sync/ with vocabulary, errors, connectors, assets, engine and inferences. Chosen because the duplication grep over backend/dsr for crm_file_id, files/2026, multipart, upload(bytes) and attach(file_id, record_id) found no CRM file path, and because the spec asks for a two-method connector interface that no existing package models.
the_shape_being_gated.plugin: backend/dsr/features/wf047_mirror_room_documents_into_crm_files.py exporting FEATURE and a router on prefix /api/wf-047, mounted by discovery alone.
the_shape_being_gated.connector_interface: upload(bytes, filename, mime_type, folder_id) -> file_id and attach(file_id, record_id) -> attachment, both from the spec's extensibility field, with upload and attach as the only two methods a connector must implement.
the_shape_being_gated.collections: crm_file_connection, crm_file_asset, crm_file_mirror. Ordinary JSON in records.data. The asset row carries the vendor-agnostic crm_file_id slot, which is what makes sync state survive a connector swap, plus content_digest and mirrored_digest.
the_shape_being_gated.revision_detection: content_digest. A byte-level change to an asset produces a new CRM file id; a metadata edit that does not change the bytes does not.
the_shape_being_gated.reconcile: A route an external scheduler calls. No thread is started anywhere in the package.
the_shape_being_gated.folder_id: Optional per connection, resolved at upload time. A connection with none uploads to the root and records that the vendor's folder recommendation was not followed. A folder the vendor later rejects produces a named failure on the mirror row rather than a silent fall back.
the_shape_being_gated.attach_mode: Both, with the note the default because the vendor's own words are 'Attach files to records using the notes APIs'. A connection may choose a file-type property, documented as 'Stores a file ID'.
the_shape_being_gated.default_automation: Event-driven. The reconciliation pass is a route a scheduler may call.
the_shape_being_gated.network: No socket by default. The default connector is local and records itself as simulated on every row it writes.

constraints_from_the_brief_that_are_not_: Domain modules import nothing but the store. Use dsr.deps. Never dsr.api and never a bare sqlite3 connection.
Records are ordinary JSON in records.data. No migration. No typed column.
Every write goes through AuditedDatabase and its audit row names a route the app actually serves.
seed(db, context) exists and its returned string is encodable in cp1252.
No emoji as an icon. Shared components from components/ui.jsx. 44px touch targets. No status by colour alone.
Tests pass alone and under pytest-xdist with no order dependence and no time bombs.
ruff check and ruff format --check pass from the repository root.

vendor_coverage.instructions: Given the spec's gaps block states that only HubSpot's Files API is fully documented and the Salesforce blob page was readable only as a link index with no payload example quoted, what should this workflow ship for Salesforce and Dataverse? The issue's own instruction is not to invent a payload.

criteria.hubspot_only_named_refusal: Ship the connector interface and the HubSpot connector. Salesforce and Dataverse appear in the vocabulary as known systems whose file support is refused by name, carrying the spec's gap text. A tenant on either system sees a refusal that explains itself rather than a silent absence. Every byte and every response shape this build sends is one the research quotes.
criteria.salesforce_base64_inference: Also ship a Salesforce connector that base64-encodes the bytes into an sObject body. Cost: the two Salesforce sentences the research quotes name a collection operation and say a blob insert needs 'more values in the attributes map' without naming them, so the body is partly invented, and the issue forbids inventing a payload.
criteria.ship_a_transport_seam_only: Model the two methods and implement no vendor at all, leaving every deployment to supply its own. Cost: the seeded demo would show a workflow that never runs, which is the failure FEATURE-CONTRACT.md calls a feature nobody can review.

verdict.instructions: Now that the vendor-coverage question has been answered explicitly, does the whole shape clear the bar: a new crm_file_sync package, a plugin on /api/wf-047, a two-method connector interface with a local simulated HubSpot connector, content-digest revision detection, a scheduler-called reconciliation route with no thread, an optional per-connection folder id, both attach modes with the note as default, and event-driven mirroring as the default automation?

criteria.build_this_shape: Yes. Every sourced rule in the spec is implemented, every unsourced area is refused by name rather than invented, the package choice is backed by the duplication grep, the default connector is local and self-labelled as simulated, and the six component decisions Jev already settled at 0.91 to 1.00 stand.
criteria.needs_revision: No. Name the single component that must change and what it must become. The six component questions were already settled at high confidence, so this is about the bundle, not about re-opening them.
criteria.unusable: The shape cannot serve this workflow and needs a different foundation.
